findings.claim: DELETED accepted a dangling link under an allowed retired namespace because exists() follows links.
findings.code_evidence: state==DELETED and any(Path(...).exists())
findings.practical_impact: A tombstone/report could falsely assert that the managed namespace is absent.
findings.assumptions: Namespace write access after deletion; no MAC forgery required.
findings.reproduction: Create a dangling retired-batch link in a deleted synthetic workspace; baseline exists() is false.
findings.remediation: Use lexists() for every terminal namespace.
findings.residual_limitations: Does not discover copies, backups or privileged coherent rewrites.

findings.claim: Byte-identical file or directory replacement was not distinguished from the originally captured deletion target.
findings.code_evidence: Original manifest stores byte SHA and DIRECTORY_0700; only outer workspace inode is bound.
findings.practical_impact: Retirement/deletion could accept a replacement object and a different lock inode.
findings.assumptions: Write access between cooperative operations; this does not establish an external attacker or real-data exploit.
findings.reproduction: Move original object aside, copy exact bytes/modes into the same name and submit the original tip.
findings.remediation: Context v2 binds file/directory device+inode; recheck parents/files/rmdir targets, reject v1 destructive operations.
findings.residual_limitations: Inode reuse and hostile same-user races still require trusted namespace/OS guarantees; not real-data authorization.

findings.claim: One-snapshot C6 contract cannot represent multiple conflicting declarations.
findings.code_evidence: CoordinatorChecklist requires exactly one record for each scope.
findings.practical_impact: A caller could present a favorable snapshot while omitting conflicting external records.
findings.assumptions: Access to multiple declarations; local references do not authenticate authorities.
findings.reproduction: Supply approved and rejected snapshots for the same bound scope.
findings.remediation: Add a separate immutable dossier preserving declarations; conflicts and cross-scope reference reuse block completeness.
findings.residual_limitations: Cannot prove omitted declarations do not exist; a trusted external registry/resolution protocol remains absent.

findings.claim: Timing opt-out and observation-versus-inference need explicit plain-language introductions.
findings.code_evidence: C6 adapter previously only introduced numbered keyboard instructions.
findings.practical_impact: A user might conflate timing decline with study decline or source fields with assessments.
findings.assumptions: Presentation review only, no tested human effect.
findings.reproduction: Capture adapter output using synthetic input and inspect the first prompts.
findings.remediation: Add explicit timing-no-penalty and observation/inference instructions; keep closed choices and control escaping.
findings.residual_limitations: Long evidence, source-path hints and actual assistive-technology behavior remain untested.

findings.claim: Local capabilities and HMACs are not person authentication.
findings.code_evidence: Secrets are owner-readable local files; HMAC key is in the same trust domain.
findings.practical_impact: Same-account actors can coherently rewrite or copy local records.
findings.assumptions: Same UID or privileged access.
findings.reproduction: Review key ownership/read paths; do not attempt real identity impersonation.
findings.remediation: Supervised isolation, authenticated administration and independent trusted anchors before real study use.
findings.residual_limitations: No external authentication or institutional authority verified.

findings.claim: Local unlink does not prove deletion of backups or snapshots.
findings.code_evidence: backup_deletion remains UNKNOWN; no backup inventory or confirmation channel.
findings.practical_impact: Withdrawal requests could remain incomplete outside the managed namespace.
findings.assumptions: External copies/backups or filesystem snapshots exist or may exist.
findings.reproduction: Inspect report unknowns and prospective backup responsibilities only.
findings.remediation: Require approved copy inventory, authenticated deletion evidence and external coordinator verification.
findings.residual_limitations: No secure-erasure or global revocation claim.

findings.claim: Recovery validates surviving objects but has no durable per-file intent/commit receipts.
findings.code_evidence: DELETING accepts a subset of the original manifest.
findings.practical_impact: An outside deletion can be indistinguishable from an interrupted managed unlink.
findings.assumptions: External actor or storage loss during DELETING.
findings.reproduction: Interrupt after unlink, inspect survivor behavior without repairing events.
findings.remediation: Keep simulated-only scope; prospective real-data design needs per-object operation receipts and external reconciliation.
findings.residual_limitations: Existing recovery proves local survivors, not attribution of every missing object.

findings.claim: Check-then-unlink is not an atomic defense against hostile same-user namespace mutation.
findings.code_evidence: POSIX flock is advisory; stat/open/unlink are separate operations.
findings.practical_impact: Privileged or same-user writers can evade cooperative locks.
findings.assumptions: An actor can mutate the namespace outside the supported cooperative workflow.
findings.reproduction: Safe deterministic substitution at test hooks; no race against real records.
findings.remediation: Trusted supervised storage and independent OS/security design review before participant data.
findings.residual_limitations: No atomic object-generation handle or cross-copy revocation.

findings.claim: Device+inode identifiers are local filesystem observations, not cryptographic object identity.
findings.code_evidence: V2 manifest stores dev, ino and kind; filesystem generations are unavailable portably.
findings.practical_impact: Inode recycling or unsupported filesystem semantics can limit cross-process target guarantees.
findings.assumptions: Filesystem reuse/restore or privileged manipulation.
findings.reproduction: Review stat binding, retain original objects during replacement tests to avoid artificial inode reuse.
findings.remediation: Independent filesystem evaluation; fail closed on mismatches and never advertise race-proof/secure erasure.
findings.residual_limitations: V2 is a bounded improvement, not real-data deletion approval.

findings.claim: Local hashes do not establish authoritative remote history/revision completeness.
findings.code_evidence: Inventory and primary-task rebuilding check preserved bytes only.
findings.practical_impact: Financial comparisons still require separate authoritative proof obligations.
findings.assumptions: Partial/stale source histories or unavailable authorized source access.
findings.reproduction: Review preserved source inventory semantics without collection.
findings.remediation: Preserve frozen financial/readiness gates; obtain separately authorized source validation.
findings.residual_limitations: No source-wide completeness or production eligibility upgrade.

findings.claim: Schema/context/MAC/sequence checks and expected tips reject bounded inconsistent histories.
findings.code_evidence: Receipt event sequence, previous receipt ID, context SHA and expected_tip are checked.
findings.practical_impact: Prevents accidental or unauthenticated partial/reordered history acceptance within local trust domain.
findings.assumptions: Coherent same-key rewrites outside assurance.
findings.reproduction: Run missing/duplicate/forged lifecycle and C5 regressions.
findings.remediation: Retain strict validation and forensic failure; never repair missing histories silently.
findings.residual_limitations: Not independent source authenticity or actor authentication.

findings.claim: START requires explicit granted protocol-bound consent; timing needs separate opt-in.
findings.code_evidence: replay rejects start before consent and measured clocks before timing acknowledgment.
findings.practical_impact: Prevents unsupported local state transitions.
findings.assumptions: Correct local schema does not prove a person understood or voluntarily consented.
findings.reproduction: Existing synthetic consent/timing regressions; inspect no actual participant data.
findings.remediation: Preserve software gates; independently verify informed consent and eligibility.
findings.residual_limitations: Voluntariness and comprehension remain external.

findings.claim: Withdrawal/invalidation exclusion and human small-cell suppression are implemented.
findings.code_evidence: eligible_for_aggregation and minimum human cell size two.
findings.practical_impact: Limits routine aggregation/disclosure, without guaranteeing anonymity.
findings.assumptions: Other released aggregates or auxiliary information may identify small cohorts.
findings.reproduction: Run baseline aggregation regressions and inspect actual-human unknowns.
findings.remediation: Independent disclosure review before any publication.
findings.residual_limitations: No anonymity certification or universal differencing-attack prevention.

findings.claim: Screen-reader behavior and accessibility performance have not been measured.
findings.code_evidence: audit explicitly returns UNKNOWN and NOT_EVALUATED for conformance.
findings.practical_impact: Cannot yet establish usable access for intended reviewers.
findings.assumptions: No assistive technology or actual users tested.
findings.reproduction: Prospective AT checklist only; do not fabricate testers.
findings.remediation: Independent specialist testing with named terminal/AT versions under separate authorization.
findings.residual_limitations: Unit tests do not establish WCAG conformance.

findings.claim: Complete local administrative references do not prove independent approval authenticity.
findings.code_evidence: actual_enrollment_authorized is always false in C6 assessment.
findings.practical_impact: False local declarations cannot substitute for institution/privacy/security sign-off.
findings.assumptions: A writable declaration can contain plausible approval flags.
findings.reproduction: Use clearly synthetic DTOs in unit tests only; generate no actual approval records.
findings.remediation: External verification of all seven scope-bound approvals and conflict resolution.
findings.residual_limitations: No actual approval supplied or certified.

findings.claim: Static escaped reports require matching primary projection, not only outer hashes.
findings.code_evidence: Recompute JSON/Markdown/HTML and reject truncated, changed or rehashed summaries.
findings.practical_impact: Rejects bounded tampering and script injection within stated trust scope.
findings.assumptions: Code and primary inputs remain trusted; owner coherent rewrites are not externally certified.
findings.reproduction: Tamper each representation, rehash the outer manifest and require failure.
findings.remediation: Keep exact file inventory and primary recomputation.
findings.residual_limitations: Local test receipts are declarations, not authenticated CI attestations.

findings.claim: Legacy context v1 remains readable but cannot authorize new destructive transitions.
findings.code_evidence: V2 is required before retire/delete; v1 DELETED tombstones can be read/cleaned without new unlink scope.
findings.practical_impact: Avoids inventing missing historical object metadata or silently migrating evidence.
findings.assumptions: Historical v1 simulated stores exist.
findings.reproduction: Read a synthetic v1 capture, require retirement/deletion block, retain original context.
findings.remediation: Use a fresh simulated capture; no automatic migration or real-data deletion.
findings.residual_limitations: Legacy direct C5 operations remain separate.

findings.claim: Interrupted atomic publication can leave a partial file that blocks automatic resume.
findings.code_evidence: Unexpected .partial lifecycle artifact is rejected.
findings.practical_impact: Availability requires forensic review rather than guessing a complete history.
findings.assumptions: Interruption inside fsync/link publication.
findings.reproduction: Insert an authored partial artifact and verify state/evidence remains untouched.
findings.remediation: Document manual incident review; never silently remove/reconstruct histories.
findings.residual_limitations: Automatic per-file intent recovery is unimplemented.

findings.claim: Retiring a batch invalidates verified readback, not every copied static report.
findings.code_evidence: A previously saved HTML file remains viewable outside the managed reader.
findings.practical_impact: Historical/copied aggregates may be misinterpreted as current if provenance is ignored.
findings.assumptions: Unmanaged copies or publication already exists.
findings.reproduction: Verify stale readback rejects; document copy/release inventory.
findings.remediation: Publication policy, explicit validity scope and correction/retraction procedure.
findings.residual_limitations: Cannot promise withdrawal removes already released aggregates.

findings.claim: Legacy opt-in C5 commands do not globally enforce the later C6/C7 administrative workflow.
findings.code_evidence: C7 adds no real enrollment or real-data deletion path and does not rewrite legacy collection defaults.
findings.practical_impact: A policy bypass outside the approved workflow remains possible for local owners.
findings.assumptions: Direct invocation by a capable local account.
findings.reproduction: Inspect command routing; do not enroll real people.
findings.remediation: Supervised operating procedure and separately reviewed access enforcement before real study use.
findings.residual_limitations: Software preparation is not actual study or production authorization.
